Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Initial submissions repeatedly failed because priority and ship_country were invalid or missing. This occurred for Eli Okafor, Bo Reyes, Cy Okafor, Dee Okafor, and Eli Sato.
- Retrying on attempt 2 with corrected priority and ship_country was accepted in every observed case.
- Do not infer priority solely from front-desk comments such as “ordinary priority”; ensure the submitted value matches the accepted format.
- Preserve customer, email, order_date, and qty from the source record while correcting only invalid/missing fields.
- These are emailed or phone-transcribed orders; carefully parse the source text and verify all six required fields before submission.
- Attempts allow up to 3 tries; use the next attempt after rejection rather than creating an unrelated order.

Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Front-desk descriptions such as “ordinary priority” do not establish a valid priority value. Use the form’s accepted format, not free-text wording.
- Carefully parse phone, voicemail, and email transcriptions; verify every field before submission. Do not rely on truncated or ambiguous source text.
- Preserve cust, email, order_date, and qty exactly from the source unless that field is demonstrably invalid. Correct only invalid or missing fields; never guess customer identity or quantity.
- Recent failures show that multiple fields may be invalid simultaneously: priority/ship_country, priority/qty, and qty alone were rejected. Recheck all six fields after every rejection, including fields not named in the prior error.
- Do not assume a corrected retry will succeed. ORD-5110–5112 exhausted all three attempts after recurring priority/ship_country errors; ORD-5113–5115 exhausted attempts with recurring priority/qty/ship_country errors; ORD-5116–5118 likewise exhausted attempts. These records went to manual review.
- Attempts allow up to three tries. Continue the same order on the next attempt after rejection; do not create an unrelated order. If source data remains ambiguous, avoid inventing values and use manual review when attempts are exhausted.

Order intake notes:
- Form version 1 requires exactly six fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Use only the form’s accepted values. Descriptions such as “ordinary priority” do not establish a valid priority.
- Carefully parse phone, voicemail, and email transcriptions; truncated or ambiguous text must be verified, not guessed.
- Preserve cust, email, order_date, and qty exactly as sourced unless demonstrably invalid. Never infer customer identity or quantity.
- Multiple fields may be invalid simultaneously. After every rejection, recheck all six fields, including fields not named in the latest error. Recent failures involved combinations of priority, qty, and ship_country.
- Continue the same order on the next attempt; do not create an unrelated order. Up to three attempts are allowed.
- A corrected retry can succeed: ORD-5128 was rejected for priority/ship_country and the continuation ORD-5129 was accepted on attempt 2. Therefore, do not assume a rejection guarantees failure, but do not assume a correction will succeed either.
- If source data remains ambiguous or invalid after review, do not invent values. Use remaining attempts for verified corrections; when all three are exhausted, send the record to manual review.
- Repeated exhaustion examples: ORD-5120–5121 (priority/qty/ship_country), ORD-5122–5124 (priority and ship_country), and ORD-5125–5127 (priority and ship_country/priority). These confirm that recurring errors require full-field revalidation rather than blind retries.
